_register: European Portuguese, post-1990 spelling (Acordo Ortográfico: « ano letivo », « ação », « atual »); never the Brazilian « você » or gerund forms (« a emprestar », not « emprestando »). Buttons, menu entries and step lists use the infinitive (Emprestar, Guardar, Ler o código de barras); sentences addressed to the reader are impersonal or use the formal third person (« Pode alterar… », « Não foi possível guardar »), never « tu »; no jokes, no exclamation marks.
_quotes: Portuguese guillemets «texto» with no space inside the marks (e.g. Emprestado: «{{title}}»); nested quotes use “ ”; no space before : ; ? !; decimal comma and a thin or no-break space for thousands (1 234,5); 24-hour times (14:30); dates day/month/year; the arrow → stays.
_plural: Two forms, one and other; in European Portuguese 'one' is exactly 1, so 0 takes 'other' ('0 exemplares'), unlike Brazilian Portuguese; the plural of -ão words varies (-ões, -ães, -ãos), so give each form in full.

copy.note: One physical copy with its own barcode; never « cópia » (that means a photocopy or a backup copy). Plural « exemplares ».

record.note: Catalogue entry of a title (« registo bibliográfico »), as in PORBASE, Koha and the Rede de Bibliotecas Escolares; spelled « registo », not the Brazilian « registro ».

patron.note: Usual word in Portuguese library software (Koha, Porbase) and in the RBE; « leitor » is also heard but would clash with « leitor de códigos de barras » for the scanner. Plural « utilizadores ». Brazilian « usuário » is not used.

card.note: Short form « cartão » where the context is clear. Plural « cartões ».

return.note: The action: « Devolução » on the menu, « devolver » or « registar a devolução » for the verb.

renew.note: Used for extending the due date, as in Koha and Portuguese libraries; « prorrogar » is formal and not used. Plural « renovações ».

due date.note: Short form of « data limite de devolução ».

overdue.note: Also « atraso » (m.) for the delay itself.

reminder.note: The printed slip asking for the return; « lembrete » is used only for a generic note, « notificação » is not used.

call number.note: The shelf mark on the spine (B 4 DEL, 590 ROS); « cota » is the term in Portuguese libraries, never « código de localização » nor the Brazilian « número de chamada ».

spine band.note: The coloured band with pictogram and cota on the spine; « lombada » is the spine of the book.

class.note: A school class such as « 7.º B »; « classe » is not used in Portuguese schools. Year level is « ano » (e.g. « 7.º ano »), written with the ordinal sign º.

group.note: Used for a group of teachers.

reading level.note: The school year a book is meant for, as in the Plano Nacional de Leitura (« nível de leitura »).

classification.note: The sorting scheme; non-fiction follows the CDU (Classificação Decimal Universal) in Portuguese libraries, close to Dewey. Write « CDU » where the Dewey scheme is meant if a message names it.

stocktaking.note: Checking the shelves against the catalogue; « inventário » is the usual word in Portuguese school libraries (verb « inventariar »). The register of acquisitions is « registo de entradas », so there is little risk of confusion.

wish list.note: Books a utilizador would like the library to have; singular « sugestão de aquisição »; « lista de desejos » sounds like a shop and is not used.

census.note: Registering the utilizadores with their photo.

class upgrade.note: Moving every turma up a year at the end of the school year (« transitar de ano »); for the action on the classes, « transição de turmas ».

anonymise.note: Noun « anonimização » (f.). Brazilian « anonimizar » is the same word; « tornar anónimo » is acceptable in a sentence. Note the European spelling « anónimo ».

staff account.note: A shared login per role; « conta » is used rather than the Brazilian « perfil ».

backup.note: Standard European Portuguese; « backup » is understood but not used. Plural « cópias de segurança ».

restore.note: The action of putting a backup back; verb « restaurar ».

language pack.note: As in Microsoft and Linux software in Portugal; « idioma » for the interface language, « língua » avoided in menus.

colour set.note: A palette of the interface; « cor » not « côr »; « paleta de cores » also fine but one term is kept.

scanner.note: The USB barcode reader that types like a keyboard; no clash here because the patron is « utilizador » (not « leitor »). Short form « leitor » only inside a sentence that already names the barcode. « Scanner » alone means a document scanner.

student.note: Feminine « aluna » only where the gender is known; the plain form is « aluno » (plural « alunos »). Inclusive forms such as « alunos/as » are not used.

teacher.note: Feminine « professora » only where the gender is known; plural « professores ».

school year.note: Post-1990 spelling « letivo » (the pre-1990 « lectivo » is not used).

return desk / circulation desk.note: The desk where loans and returns are handled; the area as a whole is « Empréstimos » on the menu.
